subject: phronima amphipod
title: This Shrimp Eats an Animal Hollow, Then Moves Into the Body

scenes.text: This shrimp eats an animal hollow, then moves in.
Phronima. A see-through crustacean barely an inch long, drifting in the open ocean hundreds of meters down.
It grabs a salp, a soft jelly-like animal, and eats everything inside it, leaving only the tough outer casing.
Then it trims what is left into a barrel and climbs in. It paddles the dead body through the water with its legs.
The female lays her eggs on the inside wall. Her young hatch and grow inside the hollowed body of her victim.
A home, a boat and a nursery. All of it used to be alive.

description:
A pea-sized crustacean called Phronima eats a salp from the inside, then lives in the leftover body.
Phronima is a hyperiid amphipod of the open ocean. It attacks salps and related gelatinous animals, eats out their insides and shapes the remaining tunic into a hollow barrel. It lives inside the barrel, propels it with its swimming legs, and the female lays her eggs on the inner wall so her young develop inside it. Marine biologists call it the barrel amphipod.
Which sea creature's hunting trick should we cover next?
first_comment: Phronima has to keep eating to maintain the barrel, which slowly shrinks. Which animal recycles its prey in the strangest way?
